subject: Post-call: Hosting pathway & SSO/KMS/log retention constraints (next steps)
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@kinetic-labs.com>, Tariq Ahmed <tariq.ahmed@kinetic-labs.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + quick ask: hosting pathway implications (SSO / KMS / logs)

Hi Sofia and Tariq — thanks again for the call today. Short recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (from our conversation)
- Primary objective: embed LLM-powered document summarization into your clinician portal with PII controls.
- Primary constraints you flagged: enterprise SSO (Okta + SCIM), customer-managed encryption keys (AWS KMS / optional HSM), and 7+ years of audit log retention for access & request logs.
- Traffic profile: steady 1.5k QPS token-rate during day with spiky peaks during batch reporting windows.

Immediate implications (high-level)
- Hosted API: fastest path to production but we cannot support customer-managed KMS or VPC network isolation — would require you to accept Redwood-managed keys and shared networking.
- Dedicated capacity: gives you isolated GPU pools and predictable throughput; supports integrations for Okta SSO and longer retention of operational metrics in your logging stack via log-export. KMS integration possible but we typically require a KMS bridging setup (customer KMS + Redwood HSM gateway) — we'll need security review.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): fully covers SSO, KMS/HSM, long-term log retention inside your environment; higher lead time and licensing. Best fit if regulatory controls (encryption keys + network isolation + logs) are must-haves.

Suggested next steps (proposal)
1) You: share a high-level architecture diagram showing where the summarization service will run and current Okta tenant info (SAML vs OIDC + SCIM).
2) We (Redwood): share an unpacked checklist comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for your SSO/KMS/logs needs + an initial estimate for Dedicated monthly committed capacity. (See attached checklist).
3) Set a 30-min follow-up next Tue to review the diagram and run decision matrix.

Attachments: redwood-deploy-checklist.pdf — high-level mapping of features to deployment modes.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marcus and Neha for capacity and compliance details.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0199
From: Tariq Ahmed <tariq.ahmed@kinetic-labs.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@kinetic-labs.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + quick ask: hosting pathway implications (SSO / KMS / logs)

Laura — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- KMS: We must use our AWS KMS key (no third-party key hold) for at-rest encryption of model artifacts and fine-tuning snapshots. HSM is optional but would be a plus.
- SSO: Okta with SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. User provisioning and role sync are required.
- Logs: 7 years for access and audit logs; we already push logs to our ELK stack; ideally Redwood can export structured request logs (JSON) and we retain them in our storage.
- Data residency: US-only, no EU processing for these datasets.

Given the KMS requirement, it sounds like Hosted API might be a blocker. Are there standard bridging patterns for Dedicated or would that push us to Private? Also, timeline: we’re targeting a pilot in H1 2027 (3–4 month lead time OK).

—Tariq
Director, Platform Engineering
Kinetic Labs
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tariq Ahmed <tariq.ahmed@kinetic-labs.com>, Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@kinetic-labs.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T13:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + quick ask: hosting pathway implications (SSO / KMS / logs)

Tariq — this is exactly the information we needed, thank you. Short answers below and proposed recommendation: 

Short answers
- Hosted: not compatible with your MUST-have KMS requirement.
- Dedicated: feasible. We typically implement a KMS "bring-your-key" flow using a customer KMS + short-lived keys in the Dedicated environment; will require a security design and possible on-prem HSM connector if you want additional attestation. We can export structured request logs to your ELK or to an S3 bucket in your account (you control retention).
- Private: fully compatible, lower operational risk, but higher setup effort and monthly licensing.

Recommendation (preliminary): pursue Dedicated capacity as the primary path for your pilot. Rationale: it meets isolation and log-export needs with less lead time than a Private VPC, and we can work with your KMS via a bridging design for the pilot. If you decide to move to stricter controls later, we can plan a Private deployment for production.

Action items (from our side)
- Marcus: can you provide a baseline committed capacity estimate and rough MLP cost delta for Dedicated vs Private? (cc'd)
- Neha: start prepping the security design checklist items we'll need for KMS bridging and the SCIM/Okta integration.

Proposed meeting: Tue Oct 12, 10am PT — 30 min to review architecture + decision matrix. If that works for you I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — we’ll attach the checklist and an action-plan workbook to help decide.

Best,
Laura
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tariq Ahmed <tariq.ahmed@kinetic-labs.com>, Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@kinetic-labs.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + quick ask: hosting pathway implications (SSO / KMS / logs)

Hi all — following up with the initial numbers and a short checklist. Attaching the action-plan workbook (kinetic-map-action-plan.xlsx) and a 1-pager comparator. Key bullets: 

- Baseline Dedicated recommendation: 4x A40-equivalent GPUs reserved for the pilot (target 1.5k daytime QPS with spiky peaks). Estimated committed rate: $12,500 / month (subject to final sizing and burst allowances).
- Private (on-prem/VPC) delta: +60–90% upfront engineering and 25% higher monthly license depending on networking and HSM costs.
- Log export options: real-time structured export to your S3 (we push NDJSON) or push to your ELK via secure connector. We preserve request-level metadata required for your 7-year retention in exported storage — Redwood does not retain long-term logs for Private deployments unless contractually agreed.
- KMS bridging: we can implement a customer KMS integration for Dedicated pilots using a short-lived key proxy. For HSM-backed attestation we’ll need a design call with your security team and our infra-ops (2–3 weeks of design, then implementation).

Next steps (concrete)
1) Kinetic: share Okta tenant details and a network diagram (public S3 buckets, VPCs, firewall rules) by 2026-10-10.
2) Redwood: share cost workbook and SOC/controls summary relevant to Dedicated by 2026-10-07 (attached).
3) Schedule the Oct 12 10am PT meeting — Laura, please send invite.

Attachments: kinetic-map-action-plan.xlsx, redwood-deploy-checklist.pdf

Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
